_comment: Overlay on history/thresholds.json for a project whose project.json says "domain": "pivotal-history". Each key here REPLACES the base key of the same name; every other base key (minQuoteWords, verbatimCopyWindowWords, eraShareMax, sourceRatio, introWords, the editor) holds unchanged. Read by tools/_hw.thresholds(project). Like the base file, these are first calibrations: the pilot measures them.
_eventEvidenceRequired: On from the first scout. Every dossier event carries a verbatim quote that richness.py checks, so a scout on a cheaper model can miss an event but cannot add one (design D8).
_biographyMinLifeStages: An episode is never a biography. Its events carry a `phase` (prelude, march, siege, battle, aftermath) where a life's carry a `lifeStage`, and four phases inside one season are still one episode. 99 keeps richness.py from calling it a life; the mode is episode, or ensemble for a long campaign told through its turning points.
_encyclopediaPublishers: Summaries of other work. Tier A needs sources beyond them.
_licenceCleanClasses: richness.py counts licenceClean (independent groups holding at least one source a paid book may quote and reuse, history/sourcing.md §5) and licenceCleanWords. Facts-only sources still give facts; licence-clean ones also give scenes and quotations.
_tiers: The base tiers plus licenceClean, and one source beyond the encyclopedias at tier B: an episode told only from Wikipedia has nothing new to say. lifeStages counts an episode's phases.
_subjectIsPerson: An episode's subject is an event or a place, not a person, so the base voice's first-name rule (first_name_for_subject) does not apply: it read 'The Battle of Hampton Roads' as a man named Roads (2026-10-18). A person in an episode still goes by one name rule, which the audit holds.
_opening: voice.md §6, the author's decision of 2026-10-18: an episode opens with its GROUND (a map or plan of the place, period or drawn from a free basemap, or a photograph of the site), not a face. images.py opening sets it in the portrait's slot with the same licence, caption and placement checks; gate.py story refuses an opening whose caption does not name the place by one of the dossier's `place` names (its aliases when it has none). A life (no domain) still opens with its subject's portrait.

l1DeclarationExamples: Had you stood on the outer wall that morning, …
If you had been aboard the Monitor, …

_pov: voice.md §2, the point-of-view ladder. l1Requires: an immersive passage is earned by a participant's or eyewitness's own account (marked ownWords, with its span), as length is earned by words about the subject; richness.py dossier writes computed.pov as L0 or L0+L1. l1DeclarationPatterns: the first sentence of every L1 passage must match one, so the reader can see the mode change. l1ExemptRules: base rules that do not fire INSIDE a declared passage (stage_direction: 'in front of you stands' is the declared frame); every other rule still does, and outside a passage nothing is exempt. l1ShareMax: L1 words over chapter words. L2, historical fiction, is not a mode here.
_writer: voice.md §2a, the writer's own sentences (storytelling.md; docs/PIVOTAL_HISTORY_STORYTELLING_PLAN.md §4.1). A sentence of a chapter that anchors no claim, outside a declared immersive passage, is the WRITER's: it may ask, scale, weigh, read or draw a lesson, and never adds a fact. maxShare: its words over the chapter's (writer_share, hard); afterwordMaxShare for the chapter whose plan role is afterword. minSentences: fewer is writer_absent (soft): a chapter with none is the stiffness the author read in the first Alesia (222 of 222 sentences anchored, 2026-10-19). exemptRules: base and domain rules that do not fire inside a writer's sentence, the way pov.l1ExemptRules works inside a passage; a sentence whose every anchored claim is kind `scale` (a sourced comparison) is relaxed the same way. specificIgnoreValues: numbers a writer's sentence may use without an anchored sentence stating them (one: 'one witness'). feelingVerbs and feelingStates: writer_feeling, a feeling given to someone who was there (he, she, they, a name, the <People>) in a sentence no source backs.
_intro: voice.md §10, the cold open: one true scene, the question (a writer's sentence ending in '?'; intro_question_missing, soft), orientation, and NO outcome. hidesOutcome: gate.py intro fails an introduction whose claims quote an outcome event's evidence or whose prose carries an outcome phrase (dossier `outcome`; intro_spoils_outcome, hard). eraCap false: orientation is the introduction's job, so the era cap does not apply to it.
_eraSentencesMax: An episode orients the reader in a people and a war (voice §11); its era context is measured over the book (eraShareScope), not counted per chapter.
_eraShareScope: voice.md §11: an episode needs orientation the chapter that meets a people must give, so the era cap (base eraShareMax) is measured over the body chapters of the whole book (gate.py story, era_share) instead of each chapter. The base reads 'chapter' when this key is absent.
_cast: voice.md §11, the cast. The dossier's people[] and peoples[] (each with `who`, `source`, `evidence`) are the cast; the plan assigns each to the chapter that introduces it (`introduces`, or plan.intro.introduces for the introduction; richness.py plan: cast_unassigned, hard). gate.py chapter fails the introducing chapter if the paragraph of the first mention carries no claim of kind `cast` about that entry (cast_unintroduced, hard) and notes a name used before its introduction (cast_before_intro, soft). cite.py book renders the Who's who page from it.
_pictures: voice.md §13: every body chapter carries at least one picture (gate.py story: picture_floor, hard). The introduction opens with the ground (opening) already.
_readability: voice.md §2a / plan §4.2, plain words read aloud: editor.py check notes a chapter whose sentences average over maxAvgSentenceWords words, or whose Flesch-Kincaid grade falls outside gradeRange ('a high-school level presentation', the author, 2026-10-19). The first Alesia averaged 25.8.
_afterword: voice.md §12: one chapter after the last, plan role `afterword`: the weighing, the observations in full, the modern scale, the lesson. Its ceiling is words[1] (over_ceiling) and words[0] its floor (under_floor, soft); it is allotted no events and takes no share of the story's ceiling.
_plan: voice.md §10–§12 at planning (richness.py plan, all soft): the book's `question`, each chapter's `turn` (what the reader wants to know next; never a summary), and two to four `observations` with the chapter that lands each and the phrases (`shows`) that carry it. questionMaxWords: the question is one short line in the author's voice, the way he would ask it aloud (question_long). The author, 2026-10-28, on the proposed Caesar in Gaul question of 34 words: 'Way too wordy, please put questions like this in my voice'.

illustrations.usdSource: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (read 2026-10-19, Standard tier): Gemini 3 Pro Image (Nano Banana Pro) $0.134 per image up to 2K; Gemini 3.1 Flash Image (Nano Banana 2) $0.101 per 2K image
illustrations.label: Illustration generated from {sources}; not a photograph or a period image
illustrations.promptTemplate: An accurate reconstruction illustration for a history book: {view}. It must show exactly these details, taken from the ancient and modern sources and nothing more: {details}. Clean modern technical-illustration style, natural muted colours, clear daylight, simple English labels only where they help a reader. No people's faces and no portraits; no lettering other than labels; never drawn to look like an old engraving, a painting or a photograph.

_illustrations: voice.md §6, declared and labelled illustrations (images.py illustrate / approve / review; the author's budget, 2026-10-19: 'under $3 for some images and then I can review'). A spec of verbatim-quoted details becomes the prompt; the picture is generated by the app's DreamSnap verb (the author's own key, no model name in any binary) and waits in images/illustrations.json until the author approves it; only then can it be placed. model: the model an illustration must be made with; images.py refuses to generate when DreamSnap is set to another, because the budget would be priced wrong. It is Nano Banana 2, gemini-3.1-flash-image: the author's choice on 2026-10-19 ('switch to Nano Banana 2'), after the first cippi was made on Nano Banana Pro. endproduct-pathways/image/models.json still calls gemini-2.5-flash-image 'Nano Banana 2'; Google shut that model down on 2026-10-02 (usdSource). DreamSnap must be set to this model before the next illustration, or images.py illustrate refuses. usdPerImage: the provider's list price per image, up to 2K, so the budget is checked before the call. maxCount and maxUSD: the story's cap (illustration_budget, hard). label: under every illustration, {sources} filled from the spec. personWords: a spec that names a cast person or asks for a face is refused: never a real person's face.

audio._channel: The podcast channel (an audiocast show slug) every Pivotal Histories episode is published to. Created once by the author; private until he makes it public.

_audio: The podcast's narration (narration.py; docs/PIVOTAL_HISTORY_PUBLISHING.md PP.2): OpenAI's onyx, the author's choice (2026-10-20), voiced in Audio Script Creator so he hears and edits each episode before anything is published. hd: tts-1-hd. usdPerMillionChars: the price narration.py reports before a render. maxEpisodeMinutes: the podcast share cap (20 MB at 64 kbps is about 40 minutes). say: how the voice should read a written form, whole words only, applied to the narration and never to the book.

outro.title: Next · Part {next}: {next_title}
outro.subtitle: {series} · pictures and sources: see the description

_video: The video's deck (deck.py; docs/PIVOTAL_HISTORY_PUBLISHING.md PP.3): an AI Slides theme from aislides.listThemes, how long a slide may hold the narration before a quote card breaks it, the narration's pace for timing, and the longest sentence a quote card may carry. The visual beats (visuals.py; docs/VISUAL_BEATS_ARCHITECTURE.md, VB.3): a new picture, map or card every 5-15 s (7 at most in the first 30 s, where viewers decide), the narration's pace in characters a second (the Video Recorder's own estimate), the narrowest Commons picture a 1080p frame can use and the width fetched, how many pictures a subject gets, how often a number's card may come, and how many Commons lookups one run makes. `beatPacing` is the air (seconds) the Video Recorder leaves around a beat deck's slides: before a slide's first line, after its last, between two of its lines (a slide per line would otherwise stop the narration 1.6 s at every picture). `wholeBelow`: a picture with no face that a 16:9 fill would cut to less than this share of itself is shown whole (aislides.autoFocus). `intro`/`outro`: the opening card's subtitle and the end card (its one spoken line, its card, and how long it stays up for YouTube's end screen, 5-20 s); series navigation, not history.
